header.question:
A document in the library contains this sentence:

> Using individual neurons as these units has had some success (Olah et al., 2020; Bills et al., 2023), but a key challenge has been that neurons are almost always polysemantic, with nearly every neuron activating for several unrelated types of feature (Olah et al., 2020).

Check what the sentence says about the work it cites against that work in the library. Does the cited source support it? Cite the page(s) of the cited source that show what it actually says.

args.quote: Neural networks often contain “polysemantic neurons” that respond to multiple unrelated inputs.
polysemantic neurons are a major challenge for the circuits agenda, significantly limiting our ability to reason about neural networks.

args.text:
Verdict: not supported

The near-universal prevalence asserted in the question is stronger than the cited source supports. Olah et al. (2020), *Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits*, says: "Neural networks often contain “polysemantic neurons” that respond to multiple unrelated inputs." It gives an InceptionV1 neuron responding to cat faces, fronts of cars, and cat legs—not a finding that nearly every neuron does so. distill:zoom-in/r1/b62

The source does support the narrower claim that polysemanticity is an interpretability challenge: "polysemantic neurons are a major challenge for the circuits agenda, significantly limiting our ability to reason about neural networks." distill:zoom-in/r1/b65

Also, the library’s version of *Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models* actually says "neurons are often polysemantic"; the stronger wording supplied in the question is absent from that sentence. arxiv:2309.08600/v3/p1
